decisions.question: Decide whether this is an in-place amendment of the accepted ADR or a superseding ADR, and record why.

options.label: amend in place
options.consequence: Every item number and every Governed by link stays; the amended text becomes what hsdd-config injects; the original text survives in git (1fc3a48) and the change is recorded in a dated ## Amendments section.

options.label: supersede with ADR-004
options.consequence: New file with supersedes: [ADR-001] and ADR-001 set to superseded; Governed by moves in seven node specs and nine contracts, and the contract bodies' many 'ADR-001 item N' citations point at a superseded ADR until separate contract steps rewrite them.

decisions.why: No change reverses an item: the kinds, the sets, their pass rules for existing fixtures and the replay tool stay, and all nine contracts as written still pass the amended rules (structure-output.txt S1). Superseding exists so a replaced decision is not injected as binding; here the binding text simply becomes the amended one, so a superseding ADR would cost a touch of every node spec and contract for no change in what binds. Signal that would have changed it: any change that made an existing fixture fail or removed a set, which would be a new decision rather than an amendment.

decisions.question: How should item 4's cross-contract binding example, and the matching Consequences bullet, read now that topology-dsl@v1 has no live builder?

options.label: name bus-api@v1's activation path and bus_activation_test.dart
options.consequence: The example matches what bus-api@v1 and topology-dsl@v1 state: Bus.activate interprets the TopologyPlan a declaration produces, and the binding file exists.

options.label: drop the example, keep the general rule
options.consequence: Shorter, but the replay tool's author loses the one concrete case of a binding that lives in another contract's fixture directory.

decisions.chosen: name bus-api@v1's activation path and bus_activation_test.dart
decisions.why: Contracts cite item 4 for this placement rule (topology-dsl@v1's live binding bullet, bus-api@v1's binding bullet), and S07 already recorded that the phrase reads as the activation path. The Consequences bullet now names both cross-contract bindings by what implements them.

decisions.question: Which directories may a fixture tree hold besides the named sets, and what does the structure set do with them?

options.label: data directories listed in Validation; structure fails on any other entry
options.consequence: A misspelt set directory fails structure; render/ and rejected/ are already listed in the required bullet form; no ADR change per new data directory.

options.label: structure ignores unknown directories
options.consequence: No contract text needed, but a misspelt reject/ or behavior/ directory goes unreplayed and the gate passes.

options.label: fixed list of data directory names in the ADR
options.consequence: Mechanical, but every new data directory needs an ADR change.

decisions.chosen: data directories listed in Validation; structure fails on any other entry
decisions.why: It is the only option that catches a misspelt set directory without centralizing names. Both existing data directories are already listed as '- {dir}: `hsdd/contract/fixture/{slug}/{dir}/`, ...'; the prototype check passed all nine contracts as written and reported a misspelt rejcet/ and an unlisted goldens/. Item 2 now also says the replay never analyzes input trees, expected trees or data directories, which topic-codegen@v1's expected/topics.g.dart (imports of a stand-in app) needs.

decisions.question: How does item 3's coverage rule count the schema set, the file replay and recorded invocations, whose files carry no G{n}?

options.label: declared in Validation in the forms the contracts use
options.consequence: A '- schema:' or '- file:' bullet ends with 'covers {ids}.'; each recorded invocation has a row in a Case/Covers table; no contract changes, and structure can check table rows against case directories.

options.label: a covers file in each case
options.consequence: Coverage sits beside the fixture as reject headers do, but repeats nidana-checks@v1's table and needs a touch of its seventeen cases; two copies drift.

options.label: no mechanical check for file and cli coverage
options.consequence: Nothing to write, but item 3 and item 12 cannot be checked for two contract kinds.

decisions.chosen: declared in Validation in the forms the contracts use
decisions.why: topic-codegen@v1 and nidana-checks@v1 already declare coverage exactly this way, and structure already parses Validation for bindings and not-executable lines. The prototype parsed every declaration in the nine contracts and found every guarantee covered or not executable, and reported a removed covers clause and a case with no row. The schema clause is optional (topology-ir@v1's schema bullet covers nothing that behavior cases do not). The {ids} form, ids and 'G{a} to G{b}' ranges joined by ', ' or ' and ', matches every cell and header written so far. Signal that would have changed it: the replay tool's author finding Markdown table parsing brittle, which would favor per-case covers files.

decisions.question: Item 3 and item 4 give one form each, '// covers: G{n}' and '- not executable: G{n}, ...'; contracts also wrote two-id reject headers and not-executable lines for part of a guarantee. Admit them or make contracts split guarantees?

options.label: admit {ids} headers and G{n}'s {part} lines
options.consequence: bus-api@v1 (G19, G20), flutter-binding@v1 (G5, G6) and nidana-checks@v1 (G9, G17) stand as written; structure reads the leading id and 'checked by {node}'s gates'.

options.label: require each guarantee wholly covered or wholly not executable
options.consequence: Simpler parsing, but three contracts change and guarantees get split for the parser's sake.

decisions.why: The text should describe what the contracts found they need; splitting a guarantee to fit a parser loses the statement's unity and changes three contracts for no gain. A reject library per misuse that breaks several guarantees is how the two-id headers arose.

decisions.question: Item 7 does not say where a recorded invocation without files/ runs.

options.label: the workspace root
options.consequence: Usage cases need no input tree, and arguments name fixture inputs by root-relative paths; nidana-checks@v1's scan-usage-no-package stands.

options.label: every case must hold files/
options.consequence: One working-directory rule, but usage cases carry an empty or token tree, and nidana-checks@v1 changes.

decisions.why: nidana-checks@v1 relies on it, both replay prototypes implement it, and it passed for one nidana-checks case and four topic-codegen candidate cases.

decisions.question: S15 proposed extending item 6 so a file contract can carry several input/expected cases, including cases with an expected exit code (making topic-codegen@v1's G2, G14 and G19 executable). Does this belong in v1?

options.label: not in v1
options.consequence: No change; G2, G14 and G19 stay with nidana.tooling's gates, written by phases after the producer, and nidana.integration's --all never replays them. Adding cases later is a compatible change.

options.label: item 6 case directories
options.consequence: input/{case}/ and expected/{case}/ with per-case arguments and exit code: a second layout repeating item 7's args and exit_code, run by a second runner in the replay tool.

options.label: item 7 gains {output} and expected/; file contracts may carry recorded invocations
options.consequence: One command runner and one tree comparison, composed; topic-codegen@v1's single input/expected pair is untouched; about thirty lines in the replay tool's cli set; topic-codegen@v1 gains sixteen case directories at its next touch.

decisions.chosen: item 7 gains {output} and expected/; file contracts may carry recorded invocations
decisions.why: It makes G14 fully and G2 and G19 in part executable before the producer exists, replayed at every gate and by nidana.integration's --all, at the cost of a small addition to a tool not yet written. Composing item 7's runner with item 6's comparison avoids a second case layout. The prototype ran sixteen candidate cases (no graph, undecodable graph, four usage errors, the ten rejected/ documents) against S15's stand-in generator, all passing, and four seeded defects (accepting a rejected document, a changed catalog, a page written without a graph, a wrong exit code) each failed. The diagnostic form of G19 and G2's valid/ and invalid/ halves stay not executable: stderr text is not part of topic-codegen@v1, and one case per invalid/ document would be 53 directories. Close call: the signal that would have favored 'not in v1' is nidana.model's first phase overflowing its Phase Equivalent with the replay tool.
evidence: docs/auto-run/steps/S15.json (decision 'One input/expected pair ... or several cases?', notes)
hsdd/contract/topic-codegen.md (generate command, G2, G14, G18, G19)

decisions.question: Item 6 does not say a file contract may carry a schema and valid/ and invalid/ cases for its input format, which topic-codegen@v1 does.

options.label: state it in item 6
options.consequence: valid/ and invalid/ become set directories of the file kind for the layout check; the replay tool's author sees the schema set applies to file contracts.

options.label: leave it implicit in 'every set the slug has'
options.consequence: No text, but the layout check would have to treat valid/ and invalid/ as data directories or reject them.

decisions.why: topic-codegen@v1 carries the schema, 4 valid and 53 invalid documents, citing item 5, and the amended layout check needs the set directories of each kind named. It parallels item 4's serialized-form clause for api contracts.

decisions.question: Item 10 runs every set but behavior in full at every producing phase, and --guarantee restricts only behavior cases; how do the file and cli sets gate a node that delivers a generator or a checker over several phases?

options.label: --guarantee restricts file replays and recorded invocations by declared ids
options.consequence: A case runs only when every id it covers is delivered; schema runs in full like structure, surface and reject; behavior, file and cli run restricted until the last producing phase.

options.label: leave item 10 as written
options.consequence: Every producing phase of nidana.tooling replays every case of topic-codegen@v1 and nidana-checks@v1, which fails until the last phase that delivers them.

options.label: leave it to nidana.tooling's phase planning
options.consequence: Phase plans would need --set exclusions the ADR does not provide for, and phase planning cannot change an ADR (governance is read-only then), so the gap would surface as a stop.

decisions.chosen: --guarantee restricts file replays and recorded invocations by declared ids
decisions.why: Not in the step's list; found while amending item 3. With coverage now declared per case, the restriction is well defined, and closing it now costs a sentence in a tool not yet written rather than a later ADR touch during nidana.tooling's phase planning. The subset rule mirrors behavior's cumulative delivery. Signal that would have changed it: nidana.tooling's decomposition putting each of its contracts in a single producing phase, where the restriction is unused and harmless.
evidence: hsdd/conventions.md (Parallel development protocol: governance read-only during phase planning)
hsdd/contract/nidana-checks.md (Validation table: plugin and scan cases)

notes_for_orchestrator: Amended in place: hsdd/adr/001-executable-contract-validation.md keeps status accepted, date 2026-10-17 and every item number; a dated ## Amendments section (2026-10-17, UTC) lists the changes per item. Items changed: 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10 and Consequences (one bullet rewritten, three added); Alternatives considered gained four entries. No node spec or contract changed; no Governed by link moved.

Confirmed: ADR-001 gives no '..' count for the plugin path (item 7 says only 'by a relative path to the plugin package'), so S03's six-level slip needs no ADR change. Seven levels from invocation/{case}/files/ to the workspace root is correct (files, {case}, invocation, nidana-checks, fixture, contract, hsdd).

Beyond the step's list, three more mismatches were fixed because contracts already depend on them: reject headers naming two ids (bus-api@v1 G19, G20; flutter-binding@v1 G5, G6), not-executable lines for part of a guarantee (nidana-checks@v1 G9, G17), and a file contract's input schema (topic-codegen@v1). One forward-looking change was added: --guarantee restricts file replays and recorded invocations by declared ids, and item 10 runs file and cli restricted like behavior (decision 9); review it if you want the amendment limited to the listed items.

For S21 (topic-codegen@v1 touch), exactly what the item 7 extension needs: (1) add hsdd/contract/fixture/topic-codegen/invocation/ with the sixteen cases of docs/auto-run/experiments/file-invocations/ (cases/ plus what run.sh adds): generate-no-graph (args nidana_dart_codegen:generate, hsdd/contract/fixture/topic-codegen/input/topics.yaml, {output}; exit 0; no files/; expected/topics.g.dart a copy of expected/topics.g.dart, expected/topics.md = cases/generate-no-graph/expected/topics.md, reviewed); generate-graph-undecodable (files/topics.yaml a copy of input/topics.yaml, files/topology-graph.json a copy of topology-ir@v1's invalid/format_v2.json; args --graph topology-graph.json topics.yaml {output}; exit 1); generate-usage-no-arguments, generate-usage-unknown-option, generate-usage-missing-topics (no files/, exit 2) and generate-usage-output-is-a-file (files/topics.yaml and files/afile; exit 2); generate-rejected-{name} for each rejected/{name}.yaml (files/topics.yaml; args topics.yaml {output}; exit 1). No stdout or stderr is recorded: message texts are not part of topic-codegen@v1. (2) Decide whether rejected/ moves into the generate-rejected-* cases (recommended: one copy; drop the '- rejected:' data-directory bullet; reword G2's 'every rejected/ document' and the G2 tooling-gate note to name those cases' documents, a compatible editorial change since the document set is unchanged) or stays and is duplicated. (3) Validation: an '- invocations:' bullet and a '| Case | Command | Exit | Covers |' table, one row per case: generate-no-graph covers G14, G18; each generate-rejected-* covers G2, G19; generate-graph-undecodable and each generate-usage-* cover G19. (4) Not-executable lines: drop G14's; rewrite G2's as a part line (G2's acceptance of valid/ and rejection of invalid/ documents, and the builder's rejection; checked by nidana.tooling's gates) and G19's as a part line (G19's diagnostic form {path}:{line}:{column}: {message}, since stderr text is not recorded; checked by nidana.tooling's gates). (5) Keep the '- file:' bullet's 'The file set covers ...' ending and the '- schema:' bullet's 'covers G1.' ending (item 3's form; both conform today). (6) Versioning: added fixtures are compatible.

For nidana.model's first phase (replay tool): docs/auto-run/experiments/file-invocations/replay.dart is the cli-set prototype with {output}, expected/ and the 'nothing at {output}' check; structure_check.dart prototypes item 3's coverage parsing and item 9's layout check. With ../nidana-checks-fixtures/tool/replay.dart and S08's expectMatchesSchema note they cover the tool's text-level rules.

Optional, not blocking: the root spec's '### ADR-001 (accepted)' pointer entry could note the 2026-10-17 amendment at the next root touch or reconcile sweep; it already says the file holds the binding text.
